nativeUnit: annual broad individual client envelope (rounded lower bound)
program: Community mental health, substance-use treatment, crisis care and recovery support
priceScope: Matched FY2025 full recipient cost against partial depression-compatible care benefits; unknown crisis/substance/other effects, not whole-portfolio or marginal-gift EV.
formula: Health = (N clinical patients × judged eligible subgroup × delivered dose × incremental mode share × average annual trial-reference QALY − full patient process harm) × local share. Patient health is not reduced by household grouping. Household resources jointly log net gains and full access costs; distinct payer loss localized once. Price =10C/(health+signed income).
what: Jefferson Center provides community mental health, substance-use, crisis and recovery services.
Its matched FY2025 reference uses a broad envelope of over 24,681 individuals, not prescriptions or completed therapies.
A partial depression-compatible care mechanism assesses health and signed household resources; other effects remain unknown.
strengths: Matched original fiscal 2025 full expense and native client envelope.
An original randomized collaborative-care trial provides an explicit utility anchor and null/adverse uncertainty.
Clinical patients are separate from resource households, with public alternatives and full burdens retained.
reservations: Broad client reach does not identify the eligible completed depression-care subgroup.
External UK primary-care trial results are not recipient clinical outcomes.
Full annual expense covers crisis, substance use, pharmacy and other unquantified channels.

sections.what: Current care includes collaborative-care clinic, adult and child programs, substance-use treatment, crisis services, mobile medication-assisted treatment and recovery supports. Reported 59,933 prescriptions are not additional unique beneficiaries. Jefferson, Gilpin and Clear Creek service counties are inside the Denver CBSA, but county operations do not establish all client residences.
sections.monitoring: Request deduplicated clients, diagnoses and completed dose by program; measured residence; comparable outcomes against active public services; patient/caregiver after-tax resources and access costs; and restricted marginal capacity. Match outcomes to the fiscal cost boundary rather than summing programs and prescriptions.
sections.qualitative: Original CADET randomized 581 adults in 51 UK primary-care practices to collaborative care versus usual care, finding .02 incremental QALYs over twelve months with CI−.02 to .06 and no difference at 36 months. It excluded acute suicidality, psychosis/bipolar and primary alcohol/drug conditions. Thus only a judged depression-compatible subgroup is transferred conditionally, not the whole community-care portfolio. Local fidelity and alternative services can erase or alter gains.
sections.cost: FYJune2025 full annual expense is $91,195,341, including $117,464 netted direct event costs. N=24,681 is an observed lower-envelope broad individual count, not treatment success. Eligibility .3, adequate delivery .7, incremental enhanced-care share .25 and Denver share .9 are judgments. q=.02 is already the average trial incremental annual QALY; response=1 avoids another clinical responder multiplication. Delivery .7 represents transfer/fidelity uncertainty, not a claimed empirical adjustment to trial intention-to-treat. Clinical patients retain full .0001 judged process harm; household uniqueness .85 affects resources only. Completed eligible incremental households have a .5 resource-success hypothesis and $400 net caregiver/adult work resources after taxes, benefits and work costs, with .5 positive overlap. Every client household retains $5 judged access/time burden regardless of benefit; intensity and high-cost scenarios acknowledge brief versus intensive services. Central actual copay avoidance and external payer loss are zero judgments, not measured absence. A recognized $76,489,720 all-program expense sensitivity excludes overhead but is not allocated depression cost. Other crisis, substance, housing and pharmacy benefits are unknown rather than zero.
sections.funding: Current own giving page links a ColoradoGives recipient identifying EIN84-0474717; the destination returned HTTP200 without a transaction. Insurance, Medicaid and public mental-health provision shape alternatives and funding incidence. Donations may support unmet needs, but program revenue or financial deficits do not prove the next unrestricted gift creates incremental care. Related entities are not added to this recipient-only IRS boundary.

costScope: FYJune2025 named recipient full functional expense plus netted event expense; no automatic related-entity aggregation. Partial depression channel benefits only.
geography: Judged .9 ten-county Denver CBSA share. Jefferson/Gilpin/Clear Creek service geography supports local presence, not measured resident share.
counterfactual: Medicaid/public mental-health provision, other clinicians and active usual care without additional enhanced service.
attribution: Judged .3 depression-compatible subgroup, .7 delivered transfer dose and .25 incremental enhanced-care share; native reach is not causal clinical gain.
uncertainty: Eligibility, completion, active alternatives, clinical transfer, client residence, household grouping/resources and marginal gift capacity unmeasured. Other clinical channels unknown.
native: FY2025 original IRS reports OVER24,681 individuals and59,933 prescriptions. Lower count24,681 used as broad envelope only.
